Saygin, D. (2012). Assessing industrial energy use and CO2 emissions: Opportunities for energy efficiency, biomass and CCS. PhD thesis (Proefschrift), Utrecht University, defended 4 December 2012; promotor E. Worrell, co-promotor M.K. Patel. ISBN 978-90-6266-318-7. https://dspace.library.uu.nl/handle/1874/260602. No DOI printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 11). Thesis of five papers: Ch.2 = Saygin, Worrell, Patel, Gielen (2011) Energy 36: 6661-6673 (benchmarking, not held); Ch.3 = Saygin, Patel, Worrell, Tam, Gielen (2011) Energy 36: 5779-5790 = the HELD saygin_2011_001 - NOTHING loaded from Ch.3 or its appendices; Ch.4 = Saygin et al. (2012) Energy 44: 1094-1106 (German chemical statistics; partly based on Ch.3; nothing loaded, statistics only); Ch.5 = Saygin et al. (2012) Energy Efficiency (Dutch FYSI 2.0; not held); Ch.6 (Dutch CCS) and Ch.7 (biomass for steam and materials) were submitted. Main file: Table 2-3 BAT and international-benchmark (BPT) SEC for HVC, ammonia and methanol (incl. feedstock, not split), alumina, aluminium smelting, copper, zinc, clinker, cement plant electricity, lime, glass; Table 5.D-4 current BPT and 2040 new-and-emerging SEC (electricity, fuels/heat, NEU as feedstock-consumption) for 21 products and 8 refinery units - BPT rows that Table 5.D-4 cites to Saygin et al. (2011a) (ammonia, chlorine, aromatics, carbon black, urea) are the held paper and were NOT loaded; Table 6-4 capture units for Dutch sectors 2025 and 2040 (heat, electricity incl. compression, capex EUR2008 per t CO2/yr, 90% capture, O&M 7% of capex); Tables 6-2/6-3 gas boiler and gas CHP for CCS energy supply (efficiency, PHR, CO2 per GJ, capex, lifetime 25 yr, discount 10%); Tables 7.B-1/7.B-2/7.B-5 seven steam technologies (coal, oil, gas boilers; small and large biomass grate boilers; biomass grate and BFB CHP) with capacity, capex, OECD 2009 efficiency and levelized steam cost. _other-values: Table 2-3 regional averages and tails, EEI sectors, thermodynamic minima, the non-loaded BPT rows, paper-mill SEC, Dutch CHP sector parameters (Table 5.C-3), source sizes, CCS abatement costs (Table 6-6), CCS cost assumptions, biomass steam CO2 savings and prices. Not loaded: Ch.4-5 statistics and decomposition, Table 6.A-1 (bottom-up SEC repeating FYSI values), bio-based materials (Tables 7-3 to 7-5, 7.B-7 to 7.B-12: products, not technologies), NPV tables. Traps: Table 5.D-4 prints no unit (GJ final/t from the Table 5.D-5 caption); Ch.7 costs have no currency year (2012 used; costs are 2009 estimates); biomass boiler 1/2 and CHP 1/2 matched to the Table 7.B-2 rows by order; CHP capex per kWth+e; Table 2-3 ammonia/methanol include feedstock; refinery SEC per t (throughput basis not printed); 2040 capex of basic-metal MEA (215) above 2025 (105) as printed; hydrogen row of Table 5.D-4 looks garbled (not loaded). UKERC cites this thesis as 'Saygin et al. 2012'.
